name: wifi_interference
title: A crowded Wi-Fi channel
description: Signal strength stays fine but a third of frames need retransmitting. Distance is not the problem here, and the advice differs accordingly.

card.title: The far end is slow to answer
card.summary: Your router and the path out to the internet both look normal, but the services we test are taking 86 ms to send their first byte, about 67 ms more than the network itself explains.
remediation: Check whether other sites are fine; if they are, the problem is at the far end and not with your connection.
Check the service's own status page.
Wait a few minutes; this often clears on its own.

card.title: Wi-Fi quality is dropping
card.summary: Wi-Fi is the layer that looks worst right now: signal -54 dBm, 8% of frames retried.
remediation: Move closer to the access point, or remove what is between you and it.
Switch to the 5 GHz network if your access point offers one.
Plug in an ethernet cable for anything important in the next few minutes.

card.title: Wi-Fi is busy or noisy
card.summary: Your signal strength is fine at -54 dBm, but 20% of Wi-Fi frames are being sent more than once. That usually means the channel is crowded rather than that you are too far away.
remediation: Switch to the 5 GHz network if your access point offers one.
Change your access point's Wi-Fi channel; the current one is crowded.
Plug in an ethernet cable for anything important in the next few minutes.
